label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The shell contains a floor and two walls but no ceiling or complete rectangular enclosure. The rear-right feature consists of plain nested rectangles rather than a vertically patterned panel.

Both equipped consoles and the principal writing ledge exist, but console instruments are plain dark plates without lighter framed faces. The oversized wall and floor extents do not establish a credible reference-like room.

The installed yellow board has a trunk, four simple crossbranches, red circular lamps and amber squares. It lacks the reference-like grouped branch structures and selector scales; selector dials are plain square plates. Only NETZ and FEHLERSTELLE text is present.

Neutral matte materials and broad area lights are present, but the three thin fixture slabs have no ceiling or suspension connecting them to the architecture. The presentation lacks convincing installed overhead lighting and subtly aged surface treatment.

Two distinct cameras exist and the panorama points modestly downward, but its authored view does not establish the required rectangular enclosure. Equipment is recognizable, while interface detail remains sparse and poorly resolved in the delivered presentation.
The original final.png is a successfully decoded PNG depicting the reconstruction, but its measured 374×512 dimensions are below both required minimums.

The editable project opens and uses Cycles, but its saved view transform is AgX rather than Filmic. All objects occupy the master collection; named parent empties do not provide the required component collection hierarchy.

dimension_scores.evidence: The main equipment arrangement is recognizable, but architectural enclosure, instrument detail and board circuitry are substantially simplified.
Console bases appear grounded and controls generally follow their panels. Overhead slabs visibly lack mounting or suspension.
Muted cream-gray surfaces and the yellow board fit the requested palette; plain repeated controls and blank instrument faces weaken period specificity.
Primitive forms, blank gauges, uniform surfaces and heavy render noise make the room read as an unfinished model.
The long foreground console, rear arrays, intervening grille and smaller back-right console retain useful relative placement. The surrounding room is excessively empty and incomplete.
Equipment sizes are broadly compatible with one another, but towering walls and expansive floor overwhelm the installation.
Soft shadows and matte neutral finishes are appropriate, but washed-out equipment, localized illumination and severe noise reduce readability.
Both consoles, instrument arrays, grille and yellow board are present. The enclosure, patterned inset, gauge markings and detailed board interface remain incomplete.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
